_meta.purpose: Library -> known crypto capability context table. Consumed by context/sbomAdapter.js to enrich CryptoFinding evidence with SCA context. This table NEVER generates a finding by itself — presence of a crypto-capable library in the dependency tree is at most SUPPORTING evidence (see core/models.js EvidenceClass). A repo can depend on node-forge and never call it.

schemaPerEntry.cryptoCapable: boolean — false entries are documented false-positive traps, kept for classifier context
schemaPerEntry.algorithmFamilies: string[] — human-readable families this library implements, not necessarily registry-exact

crypto.notes: Node.js built-in module. Highest-value target for scanner/semgrep_rules — covers createCipheriv, createHash, createHmac, createSign/Verify, generateKeyPair(Sync), diffieHellman, pbkdf2, scrypt, randomBytes.

node:crypto.notes: Alias for 'crypto' under the node: specifier scheme.

tls.notes: Built-in TLS. Protocol-level asset (AssetType.PROTOCOL), not an algorithm finding by itself.

https.notes: Built-in, wraps tls. Weak signal alone — nearly every server imports https; only useful combined with explicit cert/cipher config.

crypto-js.notes: Very common browser/Node symmetric+hash library. High false-positive risk for demo repos copying CryptoJS tutorial snippets — treat as supporting context, not a strong prior.

node-forge.notes: General-purpose pure-JS crypto + PKI (cert generation/parsing). Strong signal when combined with X.509/PKCS calls.

tweetnacl.notes: Minimal NaCl port. tweetnacl-util is a companion encoding helper, not crypto-capable itself.

tweetnacl-util.notes: Base64/UTF8 encoding helper for tweetnacl. False-positive trap: often imported alongside real crypto, contains no crypto itself.

libsodium-wrappers.notes: libsodium WASM bindings. Broad coverage — one of the strongest single-library signals available.

sodium-native.notes: Native libsodium bindings, same capability surface as libsodium-wrappers.

jsonwebtoken.notes: JWT sign/verify — HS256/384/512 (mac) or RS/ES/PS (asymmetric signature). alg is usually a literal string argument, good deterministic-extraction target for semgrep.

jose.notes: Modern JOSE implementation (JWS/JWE/JWK), broader than jsonwebtoken.

jwa.notes: Low-level JWA algorithm implementations, usually a transitive dep of jsonwebtoken/jws.

jwk-to-pem.notes: Key-format conversion utility, not a primary detector target but confirms asymmetric key material handling.

pem.notes: Wraps openssl CLI for cert/key generation. Shells out — flag for AssetType.CERTIFICATE / RELATED_CRYPTO_MATERIAL context.

ursa.notes: Deprecated native RSA bindings — flag with elevated priority if seen (unmaintained, higher migration urgency).

elliptic.notes: Pure-JS elliptic curve library. Very common transitive dep (bitcoinjs-lib, ethers.js, secp256k1).

bcrypt.notes: Native bcrypt bindings for password hashing.

bcryptjs.notes: Pure-JS bcrypt, no native build step.

argon2.notes: Native Argon2 bindings — current OWASP-recommended password KDF, useful positive signal for good practice in reports.

pbkdf2.notes: Standalone PBKDF2, part of the crypto-browserify family.

hash.js.notes: Pure-JS hash implementations, common transitive dep.

sha1.notes: Single-purpose SHA-1 — flag NIST level 0 (broken) if used for anything security-relevant.

sha3.notes: SHA-3/Keccak — note Keccak (pre-standardization) vs SHA-3 (final) parameter differences matter for correctness, not just for this table.

js-sha3.notes: Lightweight SHA-3/Keccak, common in Web3 projects for Ethereum-style Keccak-256.

md5.notes: Broken hash — always NIST level 0 / flag as weak regardless of context.

@noble/hashes.notes: Audited pure-JS hash suite, increasingly the modern default over crypto-js.

@noble/curves.notes: Audited elliptic curve suite, common in modern Web3/wallet code replacing elliptic.

crypto-browserify.notes: Browserify shim reproducing Node's crypto API surface — umbrella package pulling in browserify-aes, browserify-rsa, etc.

public-encrypt.notes: RSA public-key encrypt/decrypt, part of crypto-browserify family.

diffie-hellman.notes: Standalone DH, part of crypto-browserify family.

create-ecdh.notes: Standalone ECDH, part of crypto-browserify family.

randombytes.notes: Random byte generation shim. Weak standalone signal — nearly always a transitive dep, not a direct crypto choice.

uuid.notes: False-positive trap: generates identifiers, not cryptographic material. v4 uses a CSPRNG internally but the library itself is not a crypto-primitive detector target.

speakeasy.notes: Older HOTP/TOTP library, same primitive family as otplib.

openpgp.notes: OpenPGP.js — full PGP suite, broad and high-confidence signal.

asn1.js.notes: ASN.1 encode/decode, usually supporting cert/key parsing rather than crypto operations itself.

selfsigned.notes: Generates self-signed certs (wraps node-forge). Strong AssetType.CERTIFICATE signal, common in dev-only setups — check devDependency scope.

@peculiar/webcrypto.notes: W3C Web Crypto API polyfill for Node — same algorithmIdentifier objects as browser subtle.crypto, good semgrep target for subtle.digest/encrypt/generateKey.

webcrypto-core.notes: Shared core for @peculiar/webcrypto and related polyfills.

secp256k1.notes: Native bindings for the secp256k1 curve — near-universal in Web3/blockchain code (Bitcoin, Ethereum signing).

eciesjs.notes: Elliptic Curve Integrated Encryption Scheme, common in Web3 wallet/messaging code.

ethereumjs-util.notes: Ethereum crypto utilities — Keccak-256 hashing, secp256k1 signing. Relevant given your Web3 club context.

bitcoinjs-lib.notes: Bitcoin protocol crypto — double-SHA256, RIPEMD-160, secp256k1 ECDSA.

ethers.notes: Ethereum wallet/contract library — wraps @noble/curves and @noble/hashes internally in recent versions.

web3.notes: Ethereum JSON-RPC client with built-in signing utilities.

cookie-signature.notes: HMAC-SHA256 cookie signing, used internally by express-session/cookie-parser.

csrf.notes: CSRF token generation/verification, HMAC + random token based.

passport-jwt.notes: Auth strategy wrapper — delegates actual verification to jsonwebtoken/jose. Marked non-crypto-capable itself so it doesn't double-count evidence already attributed to jsonwebtoken.

express-jwt.notes: Middleware wrapper, same double-counting caveat as passport-jwt.

ssh2.notes: SSH2 client/server protocol implementation. AssetType.PROTOCOL context.

helmet.notes: False-positive trap: sets HTTP security headers (HSTS, CSP), does not itself implement any cryptographic primitive.
